title: Riya and the thread of love.
lines: Riya is five years old, and she has a big brother.
His name is Dev and he is eight.
Sometimes Riya and Dev argue.
About the remote control, or about the last cookie.
But most of the time they're the very best of friends.
Today is a special day.
It's Raksha Bandhan.
That's an Indian festival for brothers and sisters.
Mummy explains: On Raksha Bandhan a sister ties a pretty thread around her brother's wrist.
That thread is called a rakhi.
It means: I love you, and I wish you all the very best.
And the brother promises he will always take care of his sister.
And the sister takes care of her brother too, says Riya.
Of course, laughs Mummy.
They take care of each other.
Riya wants to make a rakhi herself.
She takes red and yellow threads.
She braids them together.
Over, under, over, under.
Then she sticks a sparkly star on it, and a little pearl.
It's a bit wonky, but it's very pretty.
Mummy gets a little plate ready.
A little light, some red powder, a few grains of rice and sweets.
Dev sits down on a chair.
He acts a bit tough, but he's smiling.
Riya puts a little red dot on his forehead.
Then she ties the rakhi around his wrist.
One knot, and another knot.
There!
Then she pops a sweet into his mouth.
A sweet laddoo.
Mmm!
Now it's Dev's turn.
He gives Riya a present.
Riya opens it.
It's a drawing set with forty colours!
Thank you, Dev!
And Dev says: I promise I'll always take care of you.
Even when you eat my cookie.
Hee hee hee!
That afternoon they go to the park.
Riya wants to go on the high climbing frame.
But halfway up she doesn't dare go any further.
Dev, I'm scared!
Dev climbs straight up to her.
Come on, give me your hand.
Step by step.
And together they get all the way to the top.
Riya looks out over the whole park.
You kept your promise, she says.
A few days later Dev falls off his bike.
His knee is bleeding a little.
Now it's Riya who helps.
She gets a plaster and she blows on his knee.
There, she says.
I take care of you too.
The rakhi stays around Dev's wrist for a long time.
Even when it gets a bit dirty and frayed.
He doesn't want to take it off.
Because it's the thread of love.
